title: Days Charged When a Cash Fill Is Re-Billed — Prescription Insurance on File
content:
Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, the days charged on a re-billed cash fill depend on the length of the cash fill, read as the days supply dispensed on the fill in the Prescriptions fill ledger.

## Rule

| Cash fill supplied | Days charged |
|---|---|
| 28 to 34 days | A standard month of 30 days |
| 84 days or more | 75 days |
| Any other length | The days the cash fill supplied |

## Both sides of each band

| Days supplied | Days charged |
|---|---|
| 27 | 27 |
| 28 | 30 |
| 31 | 30 |
| 34 | 30 |
| 35 | 35 |
| 83 | 83 |
| 84 | 75 |
| 90 | 75 |

## Illustration (hypothetical rate of 0.50 per day)

A 90-day cash fill is charged for 75 days: 0.50 multiplied by 75, which is 37.50. A 28-day cash fill is charged for 30 days: 15.00. A 10-day cash fill is charged for its 10 days: 5.00.
